Thanks again for the SIG spreadsheet you sent last week. Zenora's security team has a few follow-ups specifically around how Redwood's hosting options map to our PHI handling requirements. We're trying to close the SIG ASAP and need concise, annotated answers on the following:

- Which deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) allow customer-controlled network egress and VPC peering?
- For Dedicated: are GPUs single-tenant per customer or multi-tenant on a hardware level?
- For Private/VPC or on-prem: what pieces of the control plane remain managed by Redwood (if any)?
- Encryption at rest: do customers supply their KMS keys (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private?
- Auditability: which hosting modes provide token-level audit logs (API + pod-level) and for how long?

Could you annotate the SIG spreadsheet with short, explicit answers and any supporting artifacts (network diagram, example log excerpt)? We have a compliance review next Tuesday.

High-level summary (short bullets you can drop into the SIG):
- Hosted: shared control plane, no VPC peering; limited egress controls via private network peering add-on; Redwood manages keys by default (customer-managed keys available for enterprise contracts).
- Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pools + optional VPC peering; hardware tenancy is tenant-aware (isolated pools) — not required to be single physical GPU per customer, but allocation is exclusive to your tenancy.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed control plane options available; BYOK supported and recommended for PHI.

Hannah — notes below you can paste into the SIG. I also attached a simplified segmentation diagram we can share.

Precise wording for SIG questions (by mode):

Hosted (Redwood-managed shared-host):
- Network & egress: Customers do not get VPC peering by default; egress is via Redwood-managed NAT. For enterprise customers we offer an add-on for private peering to supported regions (explicitly call out available regions in the SIG).
- Tenancy: multi-tenant at the hardware level. Workloads are logically isolated at the process/container level; no physical GPU exclusivity guarantee.
- Keys: Redwood-managed by default; KMS integration available for enterprise with restrictions (control plane still signs some internal metadata).
- Audit logs: API-level audit trails available; token-level tracebacks are recorded but stored in Redwood's control plane with configurable export (up to N days depending on plan).

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Network & egress: Dedicated pools can be placed into a customer VPC (VPC peering or private link) to minimize public egress.
- Tenancy: Dedicated = exclusive allocation of capacity to the customer. We do not guarantee a single physical GPU per request, but the GPU pool is reserved and not shared with other tenants. This is an important SIG distinction: 'exclusive pool' vs 'single physical-pin'.
- Keys: BYOK is supported for Dedicated deployments; customers can bring their KMS and we support key rotation APIs.
- Audit logs: Full auditability including per-token logs and serving-node traces; retention configurable (default 30 days, options for extended retention via add-on).

Private (VPC/on-prem):
- Network & egress: Customer-controlled; full VPC peering or fully air-gapped on-prem install. Egress policies are customer-managed.
- Control plane & upgrades: For VPC deployments we offer two models: (1) customer-managed control plane where Redwood provides deployment artifacts and runbooks (no external control plane calls), and (2) Redwood-managed control plane endpoints within the customer's network with explicit RBAC (document which services are managed). For strictly on-prem air-gapped installs, customers run all control plane components and Redwood provides patch bundles and signed images.
- Keys: BYOK strongly recommended and supported; KMS calls remain within customer network for VPC/on-prem.
- Audit logs: Logs are customer-owned and can be retained per their policy; Redwood helps configure collectors for structured export (e.g., to S3 or Splunk).

Other clarifications:
- SLA/availability: Dedicated gets different SLA targets compared to Hosted; Private deployments' SLA depends on customer infra and chosen support tier.
- Evidence/artifacts: I'm attaching a redwood_network-segmentation-diagram.pdf we can sanitize and share. For token-level log samples, request an NDA and we can share an anonymized snippet.

Suggested one-liners for the SIG cells (concise):
- "Dedicated: Exclusive GPU pool (logical exclusivity), optional VPC peering, BYOK supported; per-token audit logs available for export."
- "Private: Full network control; customer-managed keys and logs; Redwood provides signed upgrade bundles for on-prem."
- "Hosted: Shared infrastructure with logical isolation; BYOK via enterprise contract; limited peering add-ons; control-plane logs retained in Redwood and exportable."

If you want I can draft the exact cell text in the spreadsheet.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime

Rachel — attaching an updated SIG with Karthik's suggested wording and a sanitized segmentation diagram (redwood_network-segmentation-diagram.pdf). Key takeaways for Zenora's auditors:

- For PHI/regulated workflows we typically recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) because they provide customer-controlled VPC peering and BYOK for encryption.
- "Dedicated" = exclusive capacity pools (logical exclusivity) — good for predictable throughput and easier auditability without full on-prem complexity.
- "Private" = strongest isolation: customer owns keys and logs; Redwood can operate in a hands-off mode (you manage control plane) for air-gapped installs.
